title: LambdaScope wire contract
description: Canonical shape of every message that crosses a component boundary. Two families: kinesisEvent (extension -> processor) and the wsMessage variants (api -> dashboard). RULES: (1) all timestamps are epoch MILLISECONDS, UTC, integer. (2) every payload carries `v`; bump it when the shape changes incompatibly. (3) consumers MUST ignore unknown fields rather than error, so a field can be added without breaking anyone. (4) fields documented as nullable really do arrive as null - handle it. (5) the enums listed here are exhaustive; a value not listed is invalid.

tier.description: Which observation strategy the extension's seccomp probe settled on. MUST match the serde output of ProbeResult in extension/src/prober.rs, which requires #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")].

explanationStatus.description: pending = alert raised, Bedrock still working. ready = explanation present. failed = the model could not explain it (error, refusal or timeout). The alert is still valid and explanation still holds text - a deterministic summary generated locally - so it is never empty.

remote_ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 literal. No hostnames.

first_seen_ms.description: When in the invocation this connection first appeared.

bytes_out.description: Null when the tier cannot measure it.

fd.description: Raw file-descriptor facts only. The extension does NOT decide whether this is a leak - that judgement needs history across invocations and lives in the processor.

start.description: Open descriptors when the invocation began.

delta.description: end - start. Positive means something was not closed.

peak.description: Highest value seen during the invocation.

limit.description: Soft RLIMIT_NOFILE. Lets the UI say '32 of 1024' instead of '32'.

kinesisEvent.description: Extension -> Kinesis -> processor. PARTITION KEY MUST BE function_arn, so one function's events stay on one shard in order; the FD detector depends on delta ordering.

invocation_id.description: Lambda request ID. The processor's idempotency key - duplicate records are deduped on this.

sandbox_id.description: UUID generated ONCE at extension Init and repeated on every event from that warm container. FD leak detection is impossible without it.

function_arn.description: Kinesis partition key AND the processor's baseline key.

function_version.description: $LATEST or a numbered version. Different versions get different baselines.

timed_out.description: If true the fd.end reading is unreliable and the FD detector skips this event.

degraded.description: The extension could not sample properly this invocation.

syscalls.description: Syscall name -> count. ALWAYS null when tier is proc_fallback, because /proc cannot see syscalls. Consumers must handle null and the dashboard must say so rather than render an empty chart.

signature.description: Stable hash of (function_arn, kind, the distinguishing evidence). Used to dedupe alerts and to cache the Bedrock explanation.

evidence.description: Kind-specific. unknown_endpoint: {endpoint, known_endpoints}. fd_leak: {sandbox_id, growth, window, current, limit}. syscall_outlier: {syscall, count, mean, stddev}.

wsMessage.description: api -> dashboard. Always {v, type, data}. Four types.

then.description: Sent once, to one viewer, in reply to {"action": "snapshot"} - the dashboard must send that as soon as the socket opens. It cannot be pushed from $connect: API Gateway does not allow posting to a connection until its $connect handler has returned. Contains up to the last 50 invocations and 10 anomalies (older invocations are dropped first if the frame would exceed 128 KB). Without it a freshly opened dashboard is blank until the next event fires.
Trimmed invocation. Syscalls are reduced to the top 10 by count - API Gateway frames cap at 128 KB.
Sent the instant an anomaly is detected, with explanation null and explanation_status pending. The dashboard renders the row immediately and shows a spinner where the prose will go.
Sent 1-3s later when Bedrock returns. Carries the SAME anomaly_id - the dashboard keys off it and fills in the explanation in place.
